claim: A lineup-bottom model — the cheapest model its vendor ships — will match Claude Fable 5, the frontier as of June 2026, on one of two yardsticks: METR's 50% time horizon, or the Artificial Analysis intelligence index at no more than a tenth of Fable 5's price.
framing: Two illustrative scenarios, not a calibrated forecast. Each takes one published trend at face value and runs it forward. They land close together because capability diffusion and price decline are two views of the same underlying process — proximity between them is not corroboration, and neither date is good to better than a season.

metr_proxy.note: Provisional. METR has published no horizon for Fable 5 or Mythos 5. This is an early preview of what Anthropic describes as the same underlying model, and its p50 estimate sits above METR's stated 16 h reliability ceiling.

resolves_yes_if_either: METR measures any lineup-bottom model at or above Fable 5's 50% time horizon, using whichever METR suite version measured both ends.
A lineup-bottom model reaches Fable 5's launch Artificial Analysis intelligence index of 59.9, compared inside a single AA snapshot, at no more than one tenth of Fable 5's cost per token.
resolution.lineup_bottom_definition: The cheapest model a major vendor ships in its current lineup — Claude Haiku, OpenAI's mini / nano / Luna slot, Gemini Flash-Lite. Membership is lineup position, not a price threshold.
resolution.joint_event_note: Arm 2 requires capability and price together. Neither prediction method models that conjunction: Method A tracks only when the index gets matched, Method B only how fast price falls. Of the 9 historical matches where both prices are known, 3 cleared the index at less than a tenfold price gap and so would have failed arm 2 on the day they matched.
checklist: Refresh the data spine: run scripts/timeline_fetch.py, then the /timeline-refresh skill.
List every lineup-bottom model shipping on the resolution date.
Arm 1 — check metr.org/assets/benchmark_results_*.yaml for any of them. At the freeze date METR had measured none.
Arm 2 — read each one's AA intelligence index from a single snapshot, and its published per-token price.
Arm 2 passes if any is at or above 59.9 on that snapshot's index AND at or below one tenth of Fable 5's cost.
If the AA index version has changed since the freeze, re-read Fable 5 on the same snapshot and compare against that figure instead of 59.9.
Record the outcome and the snapshot it was read from under data/history/.

method_a.name: A — historical frontier-to-bottom lag
method_a.rule: Median lag from a frontier model setting a new high on the AA index to the first lineup-bottom model reaching that index, added to Fable 5's release date.
method_a.effective_sample_note: The 10 pairs are produced by 5 catch-up releases — Claude 3.5 Haiku clears 2 standing highs, Claude Haiku 4.5 clears 2, GPT-5.4 nano clears 3, GPT-5.6 Luna clears 2, GPT-5 nano clears 1. Pairs sharing a matcher share a release, so the effective sample is 5, not 10.

method_b.name: B — Epoch price decline at 50x/yr
method_b.rule: Time for the price of a fixed level of capability to fall tenfold, at Epoch AI's median measured rate, counted from Fable 5's release. The wager's price term is a ratio, so this does not depend on the input:output mix or on either sticker price.
method_b.from_date_note: The clock starts when Fable-5-level capability first existed, not when this repo read the feeds.

slowest_trend.name: B — Epoch price decline at 9x/yr
slowest_trend.note: Method B run at the slowest decline Epoch fitted across the benchmarks it tracks. It is the slowest historical trend, not a confidence bound — nothing about the fit says the future stays inside it.

sends.subject: Trickle-down wager — midpoint check
sends.purpose: Halfway from the freeze date to the earlier predicted date. Asks whether the trend still holds and prompts a refresh.

sends.subject: Trickle-down wager — the letter comes due
sends.purpose: The earlier of the two predicted dates. Delivers the letter and the resolution checklist.

idempotency.note: A send counts as done when an issue with its issue_title exists, open or closed. Issue existence is read from the API at run time, so it cannot drift from reality the way a committed flag can when the write-back commit fails. The email is sent first and the issue opened immediately after; if opening the issue fails the run exits non-zero, so a duplicate send next month is visible rather than silent.

caveats: METR's 50% threshold is not its 80% threshold. The Mythos preview measures 1044.8 min at 50% but 185.9 min at 80%, a 5.6x difference. A model that matches at 50% has not matched at 80%.
METR has measured no lineup-bottom model in either suite, so arm 1 cannot resolve until METR publishes one.

Two Artificial Analysis feeds of different vintages are in use: the OpenRouter listing read 2026-08-01, and this repo's committed AA API payload, which predates GPT-5.6 and Opus 5 and is dated no later than 2026-07-05. Both are the same index generation, but rows carry the vintage they were read at. The headline comparison — Fable 5 at 59.9 against Luna at 51.2 — is entirely within the fresh OpenRouter feed.
Artificial Analysis does not tag an index version in the feeds this repo reads, so the read date is the version key — which is why data/history/ is append-only.
Where a model publishes several configurations, timeline.csv records the highest-scoring published one, consistently, for every row.
The two dates are not independent evidence. Capability diffusion and price decline are two views of one process, so their landing two months apart says nothing about how likely either is.
